methods.name: Projection pursuit regression (Friedman's SMART, as R's ppr.f)
methods.reference: stats::ppr(nterms, max.terms, sm.method = 'supsmu' | 'spline' | 'gcvspline', bass, span, df, gcvpen, optlevel, weights); stats::supsmu; stats::smooth.spline(all.knots = ppr.f knots, control.spar = ppr's)
quantities: predict() on new rows (inside and outside the training range)
super smoother: cv span, bass 5, span 0.3, weights
spline smoother: knots, spar, ratio, smooth and edf at R's last evaluation, and smooth and edf refitted at R's spar (df matching, GCV, GCV penalty 2)
methods.tolerance: Super-smoother runs: Tol::new(1e-8, 1e-10) (largest measured gap 1e-10 relative). Spline runs: Tol::new(0.03, 0.02), about 3x the measured gap (at most 1.2% relative on the scale of each quantity), see the deviation; yb and ys Tol::coef(n). Spline smoother: spar 5e-3 relative, ratio 3e-2, R's last evaluation 0.15 relative + 0.02, refit at R's spar 5e-3 relative + 4e-3, each about 10x measured.

deviations.note: p2a returns every forward-pass term (nterms = terms fitted) with a warning; R's object lists only the first nterms directions but predicts with all of them. Fitted values, gof and the directions and coefficients of all terms equal R's (the pin uses ppr(nterms = 3, max.terms = 3, optlevel = 0), whose fitted values R checks to be identical).

deviations.quantity: spline and gcvspline: every fit quantity, and the spline smoother's lambda (not compared)
deviations.note: The smoother is a standard penalised B-spline: exact 1/3 in the penalty (R's sgram.f writes 0.333) and the fit, df and lambda of the reported spar (R returns those of its last Brent evaluation). R-compared at measured tolerance, not to digits. lambda is outside the Check (about 6% from R's, which belongs to R's last evaluation); ratio and spar are in it.

edf belongs to the stored ridge function. R reports that of the last smoother call, a rejected trial included, and at optlevel 0 only for the first term; that is why the run at optlevel 0 (supsmu) has no edf key and spline edf is at the spline tolerance.

methods.name: Support vector classification, LIBSVM C-SVC (fast_svm)
methods.reference: e1071::svm(type = 'C-classification', kernel = 'radial' | 'linear', cost, gamma, scale = FALSE, tolerance = 1e-10, shrinking) (LIBSVM 3.x)
quantities: decision values on the training rows
radial: number and indices of support vectors, dual coefficients
properties of every run: 0 <= alpha <= C, sum alpha y = 0, optimality condition, dual objective at least e1071's
methods.tolerance: Tol::iterative(4e-7), 10x the largest difference measured in the five runs (3.3e-8, a radial dual coefficient), below the 1e-6 limit; support-vector counts and indices (radial) and predictions exact. p2a runs at e1071's tolerance 1e-10 with the rows in their original order.

deviations.quantity: linear runs: alphas and support-vector indices (not compared)
deviations.note: The dual of a linear kernel need not be unique, so only w is compared; the dual objective of p2a's alphas is checked against e1071's.

not pinned: linear_svm's select_second_alpha hard-codes the bound 1.0; kernel_svm's SMO skips alpha steps below 1e-5, so it is accurate only to its KKT tolerance. fast_svm is the LIBSVM-equivalent solver.
